edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), via Latin Wikisource
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Adam protolapsus, ut Dei praecepta vitaret, Belias tentator fuit de invidia palmae; Contulit et nobis seu boni seu mali quod egit, Dux nati nativitatis, morimur indeque per illum: Ex divino ipse ut recedens exsul a verbo. Finitis sex millibus annis immortales erimus. Gustato pomi ligno mors intravit in orbem: Hoc ligno mortis generamur vitae futurae. In ligno pendet vita ferens poma, praecepta. Cavete nunc vitalia poma credentes. Lex a ligno data est homini primitivo timenda, Mors unde provenit neglecta lege primordi: Nunc extende manum, et sume de ligno vitali. Optima lex Domini sequens de ligno processit. Perdita lex prima; gustat unde licet illi. Qui deos adorat vetitos, mala gaudia vitae. Respuite gustum; sufficiet scire quod esset. Si vivere vultis, reddite vos legi secundae. Templorum culturas, daemonum fata vitate Vertite vos Christo, et eritis Deo sodales. Xanta Dei lex est, quae mortuos vivere docet. Imnum sibi solus Dominus proferre praecepit; Zabolicam legem omnes omnino vitate.
pass_a_gloss: Adam first sinner, so that he might avoid God's commands, Belial was tempter because of envy of paradise; And he passed on to us what he did, whether good or evil, Leader of birth, we die from that and through him: From divine he himself receding, an exile from the word. When six thousand years are finished, we will be immortal. Death entered the world when the wood of the tree was tasted: By this wood of death we are born for future life. Life hangs on the wood, bearing fruits, commands. Beware now, believers, of the life-giving fruits. The law was given to primitive man from the wood, to be feared, Death comes from neglect of the primal law: Now extend your hand, and take from the life-giving wood. The best law of the Lord, following from the wood, came forth. The first law was lost; he tastes because it is allowed to him. He who worships forbidden gods, has evil joys of life. Reject the taste; it will suffice to know what it was. If you want to live, give yourselves back to the second law. Avoid the cults of temples, the fates of demons, Turn yourselves to Christ, and you will be companions of God. The law of God is Xanta, which teaches the dead to live. The Lord alone commanded to proclaim his name; Completely avoid the law of Zabolicam.
pass_b_english: Adam, the first to sin, wanted to dodge God's commands, so Belial tempted him out of envy for paradise. Adam passed on to us everything he did, good or bad. As the leader of the human race, we die because of him and through him. He himself became an exile, retreating from the divine Word. When six thousand years are complete, we will become immortal. Death entered the world when the wood of the tree was tasted; by this wood of death we are born for the life to come. Life hangs on the wood, bearing fruit and commandments. So beware now, you who believe, of those life-giving fruits. The law was given to the first man from the wood, a law to be feared, for death springs from neglecting that primal law. Now reach out your hand and take from the wood of life. The best law of the Lord came forth from the wood for those who follow it. The first law is lost; he tastes because permission is granted to him. Whoever worships forbidden gods possesses the evil joys of life. Reject the taste; knowing what it was will suffice. If you want to live, surrender yourselves to the second law. Shun the cults of temples and the doom of demons. Turn to Christ, and you will become companions of God. The law of God is Xanta, which teaches the dead to live. The Lord alone commanded that his name be proclaimed; completely avoid the law of Zabolicam.
